newsitem.title: ESTONIA: STOCKMANN TALLINN Q1 SALES 100 MLN EEK.
newsitem.headline: STOCKMANN TALLINN Q1 SALES 100 MLN EEK.

text.p: The Tallinn branch of Finnish retailer Stockmann said on Friday that its first quarter turnover was 100 million kroons and it expected the total year sales figure to be 450-500 million kroons.
"Turnover for the department store as of March 31 was approximately 100 million kroons," Juha Oksanen, managing director of the Tallinn store, told Reuters.
He made the comments as Stockmann's main local competitor Tallinna Kaubamaja this week took its first steps in the Finnish market by opening a Helsinki brach.
"I estimate that turnover by the year's end will be 450-500 million kroons," he added.
The total first quarter sales of Stockmann rose 15.1 percent year-on-year to 1.92 billion markka, the company said this week.
Oksanen said the company was satisfied with its market share in Estonia but added that it is difficult to say exactly how much they had due to the size of the grey market in Tallinn.
"We estimate that we have about 5-10 percent of the grocery market, 20-30 percent of the clothing market and about 10 percent for electrical comsumer goods."
Oksanen said that the new visa-free travel between Estonia Finland, which will start operation on May 1, would bring only about a 5-10 percent increase in turnover.
"The new agreement will not have a major effect as Finnish people have already had visa-free travel to Estonia with the one-day cruises, but it will add about 5-10 percent," he said.
